summary: Advertise NFS, SMB3, S3 and SFTP backup destinations after bounded Core gates, with Core-owned credentials, operations, health and paged complete authority transfer; final timed and browser acceptance remains open. Also removes the v0 inline backup authority format (only the v2 paged format remains) and the backup-destination capability advertisements.

guide.reason: The development NFS workflow describes Core-reported repository health and policy warnings. Backup and recovery guidance distinguishes the legacy 64 MiB v1 limit from current v2 paged source support, while recording bounded native complete-history promotion; retained runs are read from Core through authenticated pages rather than heartbeat inventory. A bounded post-promotion NFS payload backup and restore passed later. The NFS guide now instructs operators to use a new repository ID for a moved export or filesystem so old points retain their original destination; the guide now covers all four advertised destinations while the final enabled-build and timed gates remain open. The catalog rebuild guide now explains Core-local pending operations, exact retry and refusal of unresolved remote delete records.

api.reason: Changes Controller, Core-local and peer backup repository registration, typed destination sources, transient credential handoff, health and authority capability/transfer contracts. The new authenticated Core peer repository access POST validates exact member destination, generation and identity, transiently prepares a missing local record, and returns bounded access observations; the existing peer backup-operation GET now returns 404 for a missing exact operation so master reconciliation can settle an orphaned request. Controller/Core report and client API shapes are unchanged by these two peer fixes. The existing policy PUT/Core upsert now requires expected_revision and conflicts on stale updates; SMB3 rotation reuses that operation to switch repository_id; Core registration refuses same-ID source or credential-reference changes for SMB3, S3 and SFTP, and same-ID NFS source or observed filesystem identity changes, so retained points remain bound to their original destination. The NFS refusal tightens existing Core registration behavior without a new route or payload. Existing authenticated NFS peer dispatch, member access and promotion carry the master-observed filesystem identity, which updated members compare before owner-marker claims; matching updated Core versions are required because older peers derived identity from source alone. Moves/rotation use a new repository ID. The Run now repair restores the existing 202 acknowledgement behavior without a schema change. The stale-member admission repair uses the existing Core-local repository contract and adds no operator step. Core-local catalog import/rebuild now returns 202/pending while a bounded Core worker scans; operation GET and exact replay use the existing durable receipt, so local response timing changes without a new route. Controller keeps its existing asynchronous operation contract. Paged backup inventory adds `backup-inventory-pages-v1` negotiation, compact agent reports with run/catalog arrays omitted and reported flags false, bounded Core reverse-channel pages, and client GET page objects with generation, filters and explicit changed-generation/oversized-record errors. Older Core keeps legacy array responses; new Core preserves history but reports `backup-history-api` unsupported to an older Controller until it is upgraded. Removal of the v0 backup authority format: the manifest fields Version, PageSHA256 and PageBytes and the inline BackupAuthority are gone, only the v2 paged format remains, and the backup_credential_sync field is removed from the peer join response (changed contract). Core no longer advertises backup-destination-smb3|s3|sftp-v1 and the Controller UI offers every destination kind; Core rejects requests it cannot serve.

roadmap.reason: The backup milestone distinguishes implementation work from the still-open destination and recovery acceptance gates.

state.record: Pool-master pool-backup-repositories.json plus existing pool-backup-policies.json, run/catalog/pin and backup operation receipt records, and repository manifests. Repository references and retained history are replicated through signed paged pool backup authority. Secrets stay in separate Core-private credential receipts and are projected to eligible members through an authenticated peer route, not included in signed authority or Controller inventory. A fresh Controller adopts stable repository and policy identities from authenticated master inventory and run/point identities from Core-owned authenticated paged run/catalog reads when the paging capability is present; it stores no pool copy. Backup authority persists only as v2 pool-master authority pages, and a fresh Controller or member recovers it through authenticated APIs.
state.reason: Destination identity, settings, health transitions, credentials and complete retained backup history must survive Controller replacement and safe master promotion.

verification.method: Focused Go, Controller, web and API contract tests, each new defect with a red-before/green-after regression named in docs/BUG_LEDGER.md. Bounded disposable-lab runs (three Core guests, a storage guest, a disposable Controller and Chromium) passed backup, cross-host restore, test restore, retention, catalog rebuild, fenced promotion and fresh Controller adoption for NFS, SMB3, S3 and SFTP under ignored capability overlays; these predate BUG-0716 to BUG-0752 and the no-legacy cleanup. The last recorded local run (Go, Python, web test/typecheck/build, API generation, documentation gate, privacy test, diff check) passed before those fixes; the current tree needs a rerun. See the QA report for the per-kind matrix and open gates. No CI run is claimed.
limits: The current tree has no native, browser or forge CI evidence; earlier native results are stale.
The lab used ignored capability overlays, planted disk markers and zero-NIC guests; it proves marker recovery, not application recovery, cloud providers or physical hardware.
Abrupt crash durability for SFTP and S3, real-clock missed schedules, alert deduplication, real-host boot of sealed SMB3 credentials and live browser mutation review remain open.
SeaweedFS was unsupported; MinIO and S3Proxy profiles are single-node and bounded.
